TITLE: Project Status Report: Nolaor and Soramis

Project Nolaor continues to be a strategic priority for Zastama Industries. With an audit finding ID of XC-1856-X, the team has been working closely with internal audit to address the issues raised during the Q2 FY25 review. The project is currently staffed by 30 people, drawn from a mix of functional teams, including finance, procurement, and compliance. Recent focus has been on streamlining documentation processes and aligning internal controls with the revised audit framework.

Project Soramis remains on track to meet its target completion date of Q3 FY26. The project team has completed the initial phase of resource allocation and is now entering the execution stage. Cross-functional coordination has improved in recent months, with key stakeholders from operations and strategy providing consistent input. The primary objective of this project is to optimize our supply chain operations, and recent simulations have indicated that the proposed models align with long-term cost-saving goals.

Liluan Nemlurel, who leads the demand forecasting subteam, has been instrumental in refining the predictive analytics models. Her work has contributed to a more accurate forecast of seasonal demand fluctuations, which has been valuable in aligning inventory planning with expected sales. Liluan is currently working with the finance lead to integrate the latest model outputs into the Q3 FY26 budgeting process.

A number of risk factors continue to be monitored. For Project Nolaor, the primary concern remains the limited availability of subject matter experts in the compliance domain, which could delay the final phase of the audit response. The team is actively engaging with the compliance department to secure additional support and has scheduled a follow-up discussion with the finance team to review budget contingencies.

For Project Soramis, the main risk is the potential for vendor delays in delivering custom software tools. While the current timeline appears stable, there is a growing need to establish a more detailed contingency plan should delivery timelines shift. The project lead has initiated preliminary conversations with an alternate vendor to ensure flexibility in the event of unforeseen issues.

A number of next steps are being prioritized. For Project Nolaor, the team is planning a workshop to finalize the audit response framework and ensure alignment with the internal audit team’s expectations. This workshop is scheduled for the end of the current quarter and will include representatives from the compliance and operations teams.

For Project Soramis, the next major milestone is the completion of the pilot phase, which is expected to take place in mid-Q3 FY26. The project team will begin preparations for this phase in the coming weeks, including finalizing testing protocols and securing stakeholder sign-off.

Liluan Nemlurel will continue her work on the demand forecasting models and will provide updated insights during the next budget review meeting. Her team is also preparing a technical summary for internal distribution, which will be shared with the relevant leadership teams for feedback.

Overall, both projects are progressing in line with their respective goals, and the teams remain focused on delivering results within the established timelines. Continued cross-functional collaboration and proactive risk management will be critical in ensuring continued success.
